templates.task: Draw a module map of this repo the way {sidereus}/.claude/pipelines/arch-map.json does in its first two stages: plan.json and map.json under the arch store dir, every edge citing file, line and symbol. Read-only on the repo. Report the module and edge counts only.
templates.asserts: Every edge is re-read at the commit; a map with 2+ modules and 0 proven edges fails.

templates.gateHint: A command that fails while the bug is present, e.g. pytest -q tests/test_bug.py

templates.task: List what the planned change touches: callers, modules, data, public APIs and tests that cover them, each with file:line. Mark the risky ones. Read only.
Explore the code the request touches: entry points, the modules involved and how data flows between them, with file:line. Read only.
List everything that loads, calls or depends on the part being changed (configs, hooks, callers, tests), with file:line. Read only.
Classify the incident: what is broken, who is affected, since when, and the severity. Cite the evidence (logs, metrics, reports). Change nothing.
Search the web for the question at hand and report conclusions only, each with the source URL and date. Prefer primary sources; mark anything unconfirmed. Change no files.
Find related papers, standards or established industry practice for the problem. Summarise each in two lines with a full reference, and say what applies here. Change no files.

Look up the current official docs for the libraries and versions this repo uses (e.g. via context7) for the APIs the change needs. Report the exact usage and any deprecation, with doc links. Change no files.
Compare 2 to 4 options for the decision in a table of criteria (fit, cost, risk, maintenance, licence), cite sources, and end with one recommendation and why. Change no files.
Build a time-boxed throwaway proof in a scratch folder outside the repo's source to answer one question. Report what worked, what did not and the numbers measured; do not merge the prototype.
Survey how 3 to 5 similar tools or competitors solve the same problem: approach, trade-offs and what to borrow or avoid, each with a link. Change no files.
Investigate the options for the request: available versions or tools, their changelogs and known issues, and what the switch requires. Report findings with sources. Change no files.
Restate the request as numbered requirements with acceptance criteria and open questions. Read only; change no files.
Define what is in and out of scope for the request, the files likely to change and the done criteria. Change nothing.
Specify the API the change adds or alters: routes or function signatures, request and response shapes, errors and status codes, and compatibility with current callers. No code changes.
templates.gateHint: A schema lint, e.g. npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml · buf lint

templates.task: Plan the data change: schema or format before and after, the migration steps in order, how existing data is converted, how to roll back, and how to verify row counts. No code changes.
Model threats for the planned change: entry points, trust boundaries, assets, and for each boundary the likely attacks (STRIDE) with a mitigation. No code changes.
Plan the work as small steps in order, each testable on its own, with the files each step touches and how to verify it. No code changes.

templates.gateHint: The project's fast check, e.g. scripts/check.sh --fast · npm run lint
The project's fast check, e.g. scripts/check.sh --fast · npm run lint

templates.task: Add or extend tests that pin the intended behaviour; they should fail before the change and pass after it.
templates.gateHint: The test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test · go test ./...

templates.task: Restructure the named code without changing behaviour: same inputs give the same outputs and existing tests pass unchanged. Keep each step small and report what moved where.
templates.gateHint: The project's test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test

templates.task: Make the small behaviour or UX enhancement asked for in existing code. Keep the scope tight: touch only what the request needs, and list what changed and why.
templates.gateHint: The project's fast check, e.g. scripts/check.sh --fast · npm run lint

templates.task: Remove dead code, unused dependencies and stale comments in the named area without changing behaviour. Tests must stay green; list each removal with file:line.
templates.gateHint: The project's test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test

templates.task: Apply the planned optimisation to the measured bottleneck only, with no behaviour change. Keep each step small; revert any step that does not improve the measurement.
Fix what the upgrade broke: compile errors, changed APIs and failing tests, with the smallest change each. Do not widen the upgrade.
templates.gateHint: The project's test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test

templates.task: Write or change the hook as specified: event, matcher and script. Fail safe (a hook error must not block the session) and keep it fast.
Write or change the skill file: a precise description of when to use it, the steps, and the limits. Keep it short and testable.
Run the project's own test command once and report PASS or FAIL with the failing tests and file:line. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: The project's test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test · go test ./... · ./gradlew test
templates.asserts: The test command exits 0; a run that collects no tests must fail (pytest exits 5).

templates.task: Run the project's integration test suite once against local services only (containers or fakes, never shared environments) and report PASS or FAIL with the failing tests and file:line. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: The integration test command, e.g. pytest -m integration · ./gradlew integrationTest

templates.task: Run the end-to-end browser tests once against a locally started app and report PASS or FAIL per scenario with the failing step. Close the browser afterwards. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: An e2e runner, e.g. npx playwright test · npx cypress run

templates.task: Write a test that reproduces the bug and fails on the current code for the right reason. Report the test name and the failure. Do not fix the bug.
templates.gateHint: The test command, e.g. pytest -q tests/test_bug.py

templates.task: Run the project's full test suite once and report PASS or FAIL with each failing test and file:line. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: The project's full test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test · ./gradlew test

templates.task: Run the full test suite before any change and record the result as the baseline. Change nothing.
Add a test that proves the vulnerability is closed and run the regression suite. Report both results with file:line.
templates.gateHint: The project's test command, e.g. pytest -q · npm test

templates.task: Run the hook script with sample event payloads (allow, deny, malformed input) and report each exit code and output. Change nothing.
Run `python3 {sidereus}/scripts/arch_checks.py --repo . --category quality` once from the repo root and report its printed line only. Do not install tools, do not run any tool yourself, fix nothing.
templates.asserts: At least one tool ran and every tool that ran examined 1+ files; otherwise the gate fails as EMPTY.

templates.task: Measure the slow path with a repeatable benchmark (fixed inputs, at least 5 runs) and report median and spread. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A benchmark, e.g. hyperfine · pytest-benchmark

templates.task: Profile the measured path and name the top hot spots with their share of time and file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A profiler, e.g. py-spy · cProfile · node --prof

templates.task: Rerun the same benchmark as the first measurement on the same machine and inputs; report before, after and the change in percent. Change nothing.

Run `python3 {sidereus}/scripts/arch_checks.py --repo . --category quality --only mypy,tsc` once from the repo root and report its printed line only. Do not install tools, do not run any tool yourself, fix nothing.
templates.asserts: mypy or tsc ran and examined 1+ files; otherwise the gate fails as EMPTY.

templates.task: Report functions in the changed files whose cyclomatic complexity or length grew past the project's limit, and blocks duplicated elsewhere, each with file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A threshold check, e.g. lizard -C 15 -w · npx jscpd --threshold 5

templates.task: Run the tests with coverage once and report total coverage and the changed lines that no test executes, with file:line. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: Coverage with a floor, e.g. pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80 · npx nyc check-coverage --lines 80

templates.task: Run `python3 {sidereus}/scripts/arch_checks.py --repo . --category security --only gitleaks` once from the repo root and report its printed line only (counts and file:line; never copy a secret). Fix nothing.
templates.asserts: gitleaks ran and examined 1+ files; otherwise the gate fails as EMPTY.

templates.task: Run `python3 {sidereus}/scripts/arch_checks.py --repo . --category security --only osv-scanner,npm-audit --net` once from the repo root and report its printed line only. Needs the network. Install nothing, fix nothing.
templates.asserts: At least one audit tool ran over a lockfile or manifest; otherwise the gate fails as EMPTY.

tools.install: Install Node.js (npm audit ships with npm)

templates.task: Review the change for injection, path traversal, secrets in code and unchecked input; report findings with file:line. Change nothing.

Run `python3 {sidereus}/scripts/arch_checks.py --repo . --category security --only semgrep,bandit` once from the repo root and report its printed line only. Semgrep uses the repo's own rules file only. Install nothing, fix nothing.
templates.asserts: semgrep (with a local rules file) or bandit ran and examined 1+ files; otherwise the gate fails as EMPTY.

templates.task: List the licenses of the direct dependencies the change adds or upgrades and flag any that conflict with the project's license or policy (copyleft, unknown, none). Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A license policy check, e.g. npx license-checker --failOn GPL · pip-licenses --fail-on GPL

templates.task: Review the changed Dockerfiles, compose files and infrastructure code for running as root, unpinned images, open ports, broad permissions and plain-text secrets. Report each with file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A config scanner, e.g. trivy config . · hadolint Dockerfile · checkov -d .

templates.task: Patch the vulnerability with the smallest change that closes it; validate input at the boundary. No unrelated changes.
Compare the public API before and after the change (routes, request and response shapes, status codes, exported signatures) and list every breaking difference with file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A contract diff that exits non-zero on a breaking change, e.g. buf breaking · oasdiff breaking old.yaml new.yaml

templates.task: Run the consumer and provider contract tests for the services the change touches and report each broken interaction with the consumer, request and expected response. Fix nothing.
templates.gateHint: A contract runner, e.g. pact verify · spring-cloud-contract tests

templates.task: Compare the data models in code with the migrations and the generated schema; list every table, column, type or constraint that differs, with file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A drift check, e.g. alembic check · prisma migrate diff --exit-code

templates.task: Confirm the optimised code gives the same outputs as before on the same inputs, including edge cases. List each difference. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A golden-output comparison that exits non-zero on any difference
The project's full check, e.g. scripts/check.sh --full · npm test
The same command as «Verify», e.g. scripts/check.sh --full

templates.task: Compare the changed screens at fixed widths (e.g. 900, 1100, 1440) with the previous screenshots and report each visual difference with the screen and width. Close the browser afterwards. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: A visual regression run, e.g. npx playwright test --update-snapshots=none

templates.task: Check each acceptance criterion from the requirements one by one and give the evidence (test, screen or output) for each as MET or NOT MET. Change nothing.
In a real session, trigger the changed hook or tool once and confirm it fires and behaves as intended. Report what was observed. Change nothing.
Start the new tool or MCP server and call one harmless operation; report whether it connects and answers. Change nothing.
Read the change and its purpose. Summarise what it does and which files matter. Change nothing.
Check the changed screens for accessibility: labels, contrast, keyboard order and focus, alt text and ARIA roles. Report each issue with the element and file:line. Change nothing.
templates.gateHint: An a11y scanner on a local page, e.g. npx @axe-core/cli http://localhost:3000 · pa11y

templates.task: Review the changed screens as a first-time user: wording, layout, empty and error states, and whether the main action is obvious. Report each issue with the screen and file:line. Change nothing.
Review the change independently of earlier reviews: correctness, edge cases, simpler alternatives. Report only blocking findings with file:line, then non-blocking ones. Change nothing.
Re-check each review finding against the code: confirm it with file:line or drop it as unfounded. Change nothing.
Update the user and developer docs the change affects: what changed, how to use it, and any new option or limit. Keep examples runnable. Change no code.
templates.gateHint: A docs link or build check, e.g. mkdocs build --strict · npx markdown-link-check

templates.task: Add the change to the changelog under the next unreleased version, in the file's existing format (Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed). User-visible effects only.
Bump the version following semantic versioning from the changes since the last release, in every file that carries it. Report old and new versions. Never run git write commands.
Write release notes for users: highlights, breaking changes with the upgrade step, and known issues. Plain language, no internal names.
Build the release artifact once with the project's build command and report PASS or FAIL with the artifact path and size. Publish nothing.
templates.gateHint: The build command, e.g. npm run build · ./gradlew assemble · python3 -m build

templates.task: Write the rollback plan for this release: the trigger, the exact steps in order, data that cannot be rolled back, and how to confirm recovery. No code changes.
After the fix ships, confirm the deployed version is the patched one and the vulnerable path no longer responds as before. Report PASS or FAIL. Change nothing.
After recovery, find the root cause and the contributing factors: the trigger, why safeguards missed it, and the timeline, with file:line or log evidence. Change nothing.
Replace the incident mitigation with a fix for the root cause, plus a regression test that would have caught it.
Summarise what the next stages will change and the risks, send the summary to the requester via the mailbox, and stop with APPROVAL NEEDED. Change nothing and do not continue on your own.
Send the requester a one-line status via the mailbox: the pipeline result and each stage's PASS or FAIL. Metadata only, no code or conversation text.
Propose how to split the changes into commits with a message for each. Never run git write commands.
Stop the bleeding with the smallest reversible change (feature flag, rollback, config). Record exactly what was changed so it can be undone.
Confirm the service has recovered: the symptom is gone and the key metrics or checks are back to normal. Report evidence. Change nothing.
Write a short blameless retrospective: timeline, root cause, what went well, what to change, with owners for each action. No code changes.
